honesty_kicker: You are in the right place
first_minute_steps: Stop tapping · close the tab or message.
If Safari is stuck or screaming, force-quit Safari and reopen without restoring tabs.
Do not install anything the page offers · do not add a configuration profile you did not plan.
Do not type Apple ID · email · or bank passwords on that site or in a reply.

scenarios.title: Bad link on this {device} · walk through it here
scenarios.intro: Breathe. One tap is scary · it is rarely the end of the story. {scan_disclaimer} Follow the steps for what actually happened · then read when a Mac scout helps.
scenarios.match_intro: Pick the row that fits · do only that row's next move.

match_rows.label: I only read the page
match_rows.body: You are usually fine. Optional: Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → remove that site.

match_rows.label: Something downloaded
match_rows.body: See downloaded a file below · or Files → Downloads → delete without opening.

match_rows.label: A profile was offered or installed
match_rows.body: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management · remove profiles you do not recognize (keep work or school profiles you expect).

match_rows.label: Safari feels hijacked
match_rows.body: Review Safari extensions · clear website data for suspicious sites · see fake popup if a virus warning appeared.

scenarios.title: Opened a suspicious email on {device}
scenarios.intro: Reading email in Mail is usually lower risk than tapping links · but phishing emails hunt for the next tap. {scan_disclaimer}
steps: Do not tap links or buttons in the message · do not reply with passwords or codes.
If you already tapped a link, jump to bad link steps.
Mark as junk · block the sender · delete the thread.
If it looked like your bank or Apple, open the real app or type the site yourself · never use the email link.
Worried you typed a password? See typed a password.

scenarios.title: Downloaded something suspicious on {device}
scenarios.intro: A file sitting in Downloads is not the same as running it. {scan_disclaimer}
steps: If you have not opened the file: Files → Downloads (or Safari downloads) → delete it · empty Recently Deleted.
If you opened it and it was a document or PDF only · close it · delete the file · you are often fine.
If you installed an app you did not plan: long-press the icon → Remove App · delete.
If Settings shows an unknown profile: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management · remove it.
Download happened on your Mac too? Mac after suspicious download · Send the scout on that computer.

scenarios.title: Fake virus or security popup on {device}
scenarios.intro: Safari scam pages love urgency · they are theater, not a diagnosis. {scan_disclaimer} Mac popups: fake virus popup on Mac.
steps: Do not call the phone number on screen · do not install their app.
Force-quit Safari · reopen without restoring tabs.
Settings → Safari → Block Pop-ups on · review Extensions.
If a calendar spam invite appeared: delete the event · do not tap links in the invite.
Still seeing alerts? Restart the {device} once · then check for unknown profiles.

scenarios.title: Typed a password on a scam site · {device}
scenarios.intro: That is the horn · not shame. Account care on a device you trust comes before any Mac app. {scan_disclaimer}
scenarios.steps_title: Do this next (another device if you can)
steps: Change email password first · then banking · then anything else you typed.
Sign out other sessions where the service allows it.
Turn on two-factor authentication if you have not.
Watch for password-reset emails you did not start · ignore links · use the real app.
Mac also involved? Send the scout only for the computer · not as a phone scanner.

mac_scout_title: When the Mac scout is the light you need
mac_scout_body: Only if your worry is the computer too: you clicked or downloaded on the Mac · or you want a Battle Scout receipt for that machine. Send the scout on Mac · read the result in companion. {sibling_line} Full Mac walkthrough: clicked a suspicious link on Macintosh.
